q: How does a Vapi or Ankleshwar dye unit count boiler coal emissions?
title: Dye unit boiler coal emissions
short: Multiply tonnes of coal burnt in boilers and thermic fluid heaters by an emission factor, 2.42 kg CO2 per kg on Senseible's default or a factor from your coal's lab analysis, and report it as Scope 1. Use coal consumed, from stock records, not coal purchased.
audience: Dye, dye intermediate and specialty chemical units in the Vapi and Ankleshwar estates in Gujarat

p: Take opening stock plus purchases minus closing stock for the month. Moisture changes weight in the yard, so record it at the same point each time.

Indian coal and imported coal differ widely in calorific value and carbon. A lab report giving gross calorific value or carbon content lets you calculate a plant-specific factor, which a verifier prefers to a default.

ul: Process emissions from reactions that release CO2, if any.

example.title: Worked example: one month (illustrative inputs)
lines: Coal consumed: 300 t x 2.42 kg CO2 per kg = 726 t CO2
Generator diesel: 2,000 litres x 2.68 = 5.36 t CO2
example.note: Quantities are illustrative; use stock records and a lab-based factor where you have one.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
